request.description:
Pre AWB Creation lets you register an order in the euShipments system without creating a courier waybill yet. No AWB/tracking number is generated at this step - the order is queued internally and a courier shipment is created for it later (in the euShipments back office or via a subsequent process). Use this when you want to reserve/queue an order before the courier waybill itself is needed.

Precondition: the Pre AWB service must be activated for your company in euShipments. If it isn't, every call fails with an "unauthorized" error - contact your euShipments account manager to have it enabled for your senderId.

Requirements

API Endpoint Description
preAWB Creates a pre-AWB order (no courier waybill yet) according to the provided API token and the order data.

Method: POST Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN

Example URLs

Environment URL
Test https://test-api.inout.bg/api/v1/preAWB
Production https://api1.inout.bg/api/v1/preAWB

API Call Input Fields Body (JSON)

field type required restrictions description
testMode boolean yes If you want to use the API only for tests, set this field to true. Applies only to the production environment. On the test environment, all pre-AWBs save on test env.
senderId (company id) integer yes Must be an existing company ID, and Pre AWB must be activated for it. ID of company, obtain an ID from Companies Web Service.
courierId integer no Must be an existing courier ID. ID of the courier that will eventually handle the shipment, obtain an ID from Couriers Web Service.
serviceName string no Must be a service supported by the selected courier. Service name, e.g. crossborder.
waybillAvailableDate date yes Must be between today and 9 days ahead (format YYYY-MM-DD). The date on which the shipment is planned to be dispatched.

recipient

Addressing rules (all three apply independently - read carefully, they differ from the createAWB endpoint):

  • recipient.countryIsoCode is always required, regardless of cityId.
  • Send either recipient.cityId, or both recipient.cityName and recipient.zipCode together (sending only one of cityName/zipCode does not satisfy this rule).
  • Independently of cityId/cityName, you must always send recipient.zipCode or recipient.region (at least one of the two, even when cityId is used).
field type required restrictions description
name string yes Max 100 characters. Name of recipient or company.
countryIsoCode string yes Two-letter uppercase ISO code, e.g. BG, RO, HU. Two-letter country ISO code of the delivery country. Always required for this endpoint.
cityId integer conditional Required unless both cityName and zipCode are sent. Must be an existing city ID. The ID of the city where the shipment needs to be delivered. Obtain an ID from the Cities resource.
cityName string conditional See addressing rules above. Max 100 characters. City name.
zipCode string conditional Required unless region is sent - see addressing rules above. Max 15 characters. Zip code.
region string conditional Required unless zipCode is sent - see addressing rules above. Max 100 characters. Region (county/municipality).
officeId integer no Must be an existing office ID. Delivery to a courier office / PUDO / locker: the ID of the office, obtained from Courier_Offices_Web_Service_v1.2.
officeCode string no Must be an existing courier office code. The courier's own office code (field COURIER_OFFICE_CODE in Courier_Offices_Web_Service_v1.2). Alternative to officeId.
streetName string yes Max 100 characters. Always required, even when officeId or officeCode is sent (unlike the createAWB endpoint, where it becomes optional in that case). Name of the street - e.g. Main street or Main street 10.
buildingNumber integer no Number of the street/building - e.g. 10.
addressText string no Max 100 characters. Additional address information - e.g. bl. 25, et. 3.
contactPerson string no Max 100 characters. Contact person. Usually the same as the name of the recipient.
phoneNumber string yes Max 100 characters. Phone number of the recipient.
email string no Must be a valid email format if sent (unlike createAWB, where the email field isn't validated at all). Email of the recipient.

awb

field type required restrictions description
parcels integer yes Min 0. Number of parcels.
envelopes integer yes Min 0. Number of envelopes. Usually 0.
totalWeight numeric yes Min 0.5 kg. Total weight of the shipment in kg. Note the minimum is higher than on createAWB (0.01 kg there).
declaredValue numeric no Min 0. Insurance amount of the shipment.
bankRepayment numeric no Min 0. COD amount of the shipment in local currency.
otherRepayment string no Max 100 characters. Additional information to COD.
observations string no Max 100 characters. Additional information about the shipment/products (notes).
openPackage boolean no Check up the shipment before pay.
saturdayDelivery boolean no Saturday delivery.
referenceNumber string yes Max 100 characters. Must be unique to avoid duplicate orders! Client reference number.
products string no Max 1000 characters. The content of the shipment as free text, e.g. product1 product2.
fragile boolean no Marker whether the content is fragile.
productsInfo string no Max 2000 characters. Note the exact key is productsInfo (capital I) - a lowercase productsinfo is silently ignored by validation. Additional product information.
generateInoutLabelNum boolean no When set to true, an INOUT label number is generated for the order - see Pre_AWB_Creation_INOUT_LABEL_Web_Service-v1.1.

awb.packages

Optional array.

field type required restrictions description
dimensions.width numeric no Min 0.1. Width of the specific parcel in cm.
dimensions.height numeric no Min 0.1. Height of the specific parcel in cm.
dimensions.length numeric no Min 0.1. Length of the specific parcel in cm.
weight numeric no Min 0.001. Weight of the specific parcel in kg.

products (top-level array)

Optional, and only lightly validated on this endpoint (only qty is checked - refNumber/price are not). For richer product data, prefer awb.products / awb.productsInfo above.

field type required restrictions description
qty integer no Min 1 (only enforced when the products array/item is sent). Quantity of the product.

Not supported on this endpoint: unlike createAWB, Pre AWB does not accept/validate awb.document, sender, invoice, customsData, customs_declaration, courierRequest, returnLabel, courierReturnAWB or warehouseInfo. Sending them has no effect - configure those aspects on the real shipment once it is created from the order.

API Response (Output Fields)

On success the service returns HTTP 201 with:

Field Description
orderId Internal ID of the created order (no courier AWB exists yet).
error Always false on success.
code Always 201 on success.
inoutLabelNum Present only when awb.generateInoutLabelNum was sent as true - see Pre_AWB_Creation_INOUT_LABEL_Web_Service-v1.1.

Example:

{
    "orderId": 4815162,
    "error": false,
    "code": 201
}

On a business/processing error (e.g. the order could not be created for a reason surfaced after your input passed validation), the response has this shape, with the HTTP status equal to the code value:

{
    "orderId": null,
    "inoutLabelNum": null,
    "error": "error text",
    "code": 422
}

On a plain input-validation error (a required field missing, a value failing the rules in the tables above), the response is the simpler shape used across the API, with HTTP 400:

{
    "error": "error text"
}

HTTP Errors:

Code Description
201 Order created successfully.
400 Bad request / input validation failed - body is {"error": "..."}.
401 Unauthenticated. API expects a header like - 'Authorization: Bearer (api_token)'.
404 Not found data.
422 Unprocessable Entity - business error while creating the order (e.g. courier/config issue). Body follows the orderId/error/code shape above.
500 Internal Server Error, or Pre AWB not activated for this senderId ("This action is unauthorized."), or missing/invalid senderId.

request.description:
This is the same endpoint and validation as Pre_AWB_Creation_Web_Service-v1.0 (it creates an order in euShipments without a courier waybill yet). This page highlights the additional awb.generateInoutLabelNum flag: when sent as true, the order also gets an internal 17-digit INOUT label number that you can print immediately via Pre_AWB_INOUT_LABEL_Web_Service_v1.0 / Pre_AWB_INOUT_LABEL_BY_NUM_Web_Service_v1.0, before any courier waybill exists for the order.

Precondition: the Pre AWB service must be activated for your company in euShipments. If it isn't, every call fails with an "unauthorized" error - contact your euShipments account manager to have it enabled for your senderId.

Requirements

API Endpoint Description
preAWB Creates a pre-AWB order (no courier waybill yet) and, when requested, an INOUT label number for it.

Method: POST Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN

Example URLs

Environment URL
Test https://test-api.inout.bg/api/v1/preAWB
Production https://api1.inout.bg/api/v1/preAWB

API Call Input Fields Body (JSON)

All fields are identical to Pre_AWB_Creation_Web_Service-v1.0 - see that page for the full field-by-field reference (testMode, senderId, courierId, serviceName, waybillAvailableDate, recipient., awb., awb.packages., products.). Only the extra flag is shown below.

field type required restrictions description
awb.generateInoutLabelNum boolean yes (for this variant) Set to true. Requests generation of an internal INOUT label number for the order, returned as inoutLabelNum in the response.

Reminder - addressing rules for recipient (same as the base endpoint):

  • recipient.countryIsoCode is always required, regardless of cityId.
  • Send either recipient.cityId, or both recipient.cityName and recipient.zipCode together.
  • Independently of cityId/cityName, always send recipient.zipCode or recipient.region (at least one of the two).
  • recipient.streetName is always required, even when officeId or officeCode is sent.

API Response (Output Fields)

On success the service returns HTTP 201 with:

Field Description
orderId Internal ID of the created order (no courier AWB exists yet).
error Always false on success.
code Always 201 on success.
inoutLabelNum 17-digit internal label number, format 33333330######### (33333330000000000 + internal record id). Use it with Pre_AWB_INOUT_LABEL_BY_NUM_Web_Service_v1.0 to print the label, or use orderId with Pre_AWB_INOUT_LABEL_Web_Service_v1.0.

Example:

{
    "orderId": 4815162,
    "error": false,
    "code": 201,
    "inoutLabelNum": "33333330004815162"
}

On a business/processing error, the response follows the orderId/error/code shape, with the HTTP status equal to the code value, and inoutLabelNum always present as null:

{
    "orderId": null,
    "inoutLabelNum": null,
    "error": "error text",
    "code": 422
}

On a plain input-validation error (a required field missing, a value failing the rules), the response is the simpler shape used across the API, with HTTP 400:

{
    "error": "error text"
}

HTTP Errors:

Code Description
201 Order (and INOUT label number) created successfully.
400 Bad request / input validation failed - body is {"error": "..."}.
401 Unauthenticated. API expects a header like - 'Authorization: Bearer (api_token)'.
404 Not found data.
422 Unprocessable Entity - business error while creating the order. Body follows the orderId/error/code shape above.
500 Internal Server Error, or Pre AWB not activated for this senderId ("This action is unauthorized."), or missing/invalid senderId.

Prints (retrieves) the INOUT label for a pre-AWB order, identified by the order's internal orderId (the value returned by Pre_AWB_Creation_INOUT_LABEL_Web_Service-v1.1 in the orderId field, for an order that was created with awb.generateInoutLabelNum: true). No courier waybill needs to exist yet - this label is generated purely from the pre-AWB order data.

If you only have the 17-digit inoutLabelNum (not the internal orderId), use Pre_AWB_INOUT_LABEL_BY_NUM_Web_Service_v1.0 instead.

  • If the response is an EMPTY ARRAY, the company has no couriers activated yet — please contact euShipments to add couriers to your client account.
  • If you request a company ID that does not belong to your account (or does not exist), the service returns HTTP 422 with {"error":"You do not have access to couriers. Please contact an InOut employee."}.

Test environment https://test-api.inout.bg/api/v1/couriers/333

TO_OFFICE If this field is true, you can create shipments to an office with this courier.
TO_ADDRESS If this field is true, you can create shipments to an address with this courier.
COUNTRY Country where the carrier operates.
CURRENCY Local currency of the country. May be null.

[

 }
]

Shipment creation guidelines

Phone format requirements:

Romania (all carriers) - phone number without country phone prefix; Bulgaria - phone number without country phone prefix; Greece - phone number without country phone prefix; Poland - phone number without country phone prefix; Czech Republic - country phone prefix +420 or 00420 + valid mobile number (9 digits); Hungary - country phone prefix +36 or 0036 + valid mobile number (9 digits); Slovakia - country phone prefix +421 or 00421 + valid mobile number (9 digits); Croatia - country phone prefix +385 or 00385 + valid mobile number (9 digits).

Warning: Send exactly ONE international prefix. Do not combine the national trunk prefix with the country code — for example, a Hungarian number sent as "0036" + "06..." (i.e. the national "06..." form concatenated after the country code) will be misread and may be rejected as a landline/invalid number. Strip the national prefix first: 06 30 123 4567 must be sent as 0036301234567 (or +36301234567).

Delivery to a courier office / parcel locker (PUDO):

1. Download the office nomenclature from https://api1.inout.bg/api/v1/offices-by-courier/{courierId} (see the Courier Offices Web Service).

2. Submit the shipment request in one of the following ways:

2.1 Recommended: in the "officeId" field, submit the "ID" value from our nomenclature. This is the most reliable option. Alternatively, you can submit the office code in the "officeCode" field.

2.2 In the "streetName" field, submit the keyword office + "OFFICE_NAME" from our nomenclature. Important: the word "office" must be at the very START of the streetName field (e.g. "office Aidemir").

2.3 In the "streetName" field, submit the keyword office + "ADDRESS" from our nomenclature. Important: the word "office" must be at the very START of the streetName field.

Sample data for the points described above:

2.1 (recommended — by officeId)

``` json "recipient": { "name": "Test User", "countryIsoCode": "BG", "cityId": null, "region": null, "cityName": "Aidemir", "zipCode": "7538", "streetName": "", "buildingNumber": 0, "officeId": 1297, "officeCode": "", "addressText": "additional text, address test", "contactPerson": "Test User", "phoneNumber": "0889000000", "email": "test@example.com" }

2.2 (by office name in streetName)

"recipient": { "name": "Test User", "countryIsoCode": "BG", "cityId": null, "region": null, "cityName": "Aidemir", "zipCode": "7538", "streetName": "office Aidemir", "buildingNumber": 0, "officeId": null, "officeCode": "", "addressText": "additional text, address test", "contactPerson": "Test User", "phoneNumber": "0889000000", "email": "test@example.com" }

2.3 (by office address in streetName)

"recipient": { "name": "Test User", "countryIsoCode": "BG", "cityId": null, "region": null, "cityName": "Aidemir", "zipCode": "7538", "streetName": "office Aidemir kv. Delenkite ul. Sofia №7", "buildingNumber": 0, "officeId": null, "officeCode": "", "addressText": "additional text, address test", "contactPerson": "Test User", "phoneNumber": "0889000000", "email": "test@example.com" }

Note: fields without a value should be sent as JSON null (e.g. "region": null), not as the string "null".
